title: Model-specific precision SLO and rollback playbook for quantized variants
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: As we onboard quantized model variants to reduce cost, we need an SLO/acceptance framework that measures not only latency and availability but also 'precision' — a model-specific quality metric that captures task-relevant degradation (e.g., instruction-following correctness, embedding similarity, hallucination rate). Quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) can reduce throughput cost but sometimes produce subtle regressions that are not visible in raw token latency metrics. This ticket defines requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates and rollback triggers for shipping quantized variants across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Goals:
- Define a small, measurable set of precision SLOs per model family (chat, completions, embeddings).
- Specify automated canary rollout thresholds and staged ramping policy.
- Provide a deterministic rollback and mitigation playbook tied to error budget burn and quality regressions.
- Integrate monitoring and alerting targets and create a lightweight evaluation harness for ongoing quality checks.

Out of scope: full rework of evaluation infra, per-customer contract changes for Dedicated (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: For each model family (chat, text-gen, embeddings) define a precision SLO metric (single-line description + measurement method) documented in PRD scoping table.

Baseline established: acceptable delta between float baseline and quantized variant must be <= 2% for the primary metric (e.g., instruction accuracy for chat, MRR for reranking, cosine drop for embeddings) over the canonical test set.
Latency and availability SLOs for quantized variant must meet existing service envelopes: p95 latency within 10% of baseline and availability >= 99.5% in canary region.
Canary guardrails: no single canary run may exceed a precision delta of 3% or burn > 20% of a 7-day error budget; otherwise the variant is automatically halted and routed to baseline model.
Automated monitoring in Console created: model-quality dashboard, canary comparison panel, alert rules triggered on metric regression or accelerated error budget burn.
Rollback playbook documented and tested with a dry-run in staging including steps, runbooks and PR/automation links.
Stakeholder signoff (PM, Eng, Design/DevEx) recorded in comments with approvals before production ramp beyond 5% traffic.
success_metrics: Quantized variants deployed to production with cost-per-token reduction >= 20% without breaching precision SLOs.
No customer-facing incidents caused by quality regressions in first 6 weeks after ramp (defined as P0/P1 SEV with root cause tied to quantized model behavior).
Canary gates catch regressions: >= 90% of simulated regressions are detected by automated alerts in staging runs.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (staging): run full evaluation harness on canonical prompt set; report cross-metric diff and store artifact at CONFLUENCE:Serving/PM-15937/baseline-vs-quantized.
Stage 1 (internal canary): route 0.5% traffic from internal tenants in one region for 48 hours; require green canary metrics for 48h to proceed.
Stage 2 (partial public canary): ramp to 5% traffic across 2 regions over 72 hours if canary metrics stable. Automated rollback triggers evaluated continuously.
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): increase to 25% over 7 days with daily quality checks; each 5x increase requires no canary alarms and <= 50% error budget burn in 24h windows.
Stage 4 (full rollout): open to 100% only after 14 days of stable metrics and written approval from SRE and PM.
monitoring_dashboards: CONSOLE: ModelQuality/PM-15937 - per-model precision deltas vs baseline
CONSOLE: Canary/PM-15937 - canary burn rate, p95 latency comparison, error budget telemetry
ALERT: model-precision-regression-quantized - Fires when precision delta > 3% OR sustained cosine drop > 0.04
LOGS: GitHub PR #3456 (quantized-inference) and CI artifacts linked in PR description
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Accept up to 2% measured precision delta in exchange for ~20-30% cost reduction on high-throughput workloads. This acknowledges occasional non-deterministic failure modes but keeps user-facing regressions tightly bounded.
Decision: Use model-family canonical test sets (curated by Applied ML) rather than full user traffic A/B for initial gates to avoid exposing customers to regressions.
Decision: Canary error budget partitioned by tenant class; high-value tenants (Dedicated) are excluded from initial public canary unless explicitly opted-in.
